family.description: This family of RNA ligases ([ec:6.5.1.3]) join 2',3'-cyclic phosphate and 5'-OH ends. They catalyse the splicing of tRNA and may also participate in tRNA repair and recovery from stress-induced RNA damage [[cite:PUB00152168],[cite:PUB00057853],[cite:PUB00056744]].
family.name: tRNA-splicing ligase RtcB

causal_graphs.context: The 2012 PNAS Figure 4B assay uses 10 uL, 50 mM Tris pH 8.0, 2 mM MnCl2, 10 uM alpha-32P-GTP and 5 uM RtcB at 37 C for 1 min. SDS-PAGE and autoradiography measure protein labeling. H337A/N/Q variants and the protein-loading gel are controls. GTP, manganese and enzyme are joint inputs.

evidence.explanation: Visually inspected Figure 4A-B establishes protein loading and WT-specific labeling; Figure 2 and MS/MS Results support the adduct interpretation with the caption discrepancy retained.
Reference sequence, exact experimental peptide match and cited tag-removal protocol support member/domain mapping, not an independently verified cloning-template strain.

edges.mechanism: GTP-derived label becomes an SDS-resistant RtcB adduct in the manganese-containing reaction. Peptide analysis and H337 substitutions support a histidinyl-GMP assignment, without resolving every bond-making microstep.
edges.subject: rtcb-with-gtp-manganese

causal_graphs.family_mapping: The paper's 408-aa E. coli RtcB maps to reference P46850, sequence version 3, rtcB/yhgL, b3421, PF01139 at 29-408. The reported MS peptide 325-341 exactly matches the reference and contains H337. The reference is K12; the exact cloning-template strain and full final clone sequence remain unverified, so graph taxonomy is E. coli species rather than an asserted experimental K12 strain.
causal_graphs.limitations: Peptide mass and mutation evidence support the H337 assignment, but the graph does not assert a directly observed transition state. Figure 2's image and Results give m/z about 723.93 while its HTML caption transposes this to 732.92-732.94; no raw spectrum was reprocessed. The source's DNA-guanylylation assay is not relabeled as RNA chemistry or joined to this graph as a directly tracked molecule.

nodes.label: Tag-free E. coli RtcB exposed to GTP and Mn2+

causal_graphs.scope: Full-length recombinant E. coli RtcB, purified after His10-Smt3 tag removal; a protein-adduct assay, not an isolated domain or a cellular RNA-repair phenotype.
causal_graphs.title: Purified E. coli RtcB forms a covalent guanylate adduct

causal_graphs.context: The 2012 NAR Figure 7 plus-GTP time course uses 50 mM Tris pH 8.0, 2 mM MnCl2, 100 uM GTP, 1 uM RtcB and 0.1 uM labeled RNA at 37 C. RNase T1 digestion and urea-PAGE resolve terminal products over 0-120 s. RtcB, GTP and manganese are present together for both edges.

evidence.explanation: Visually inspected Figure 7A-B supports hydrolysis in the plus-GTP time course, retaining initial 3'-phosphate contamination and the separate control-label discrepancy. No absolute absence of slow GTP-free hydrolysis is claimed.
evidence.snippet: being converted predominantly to the more rapidly migrating

edges.mechanism: In the joint RtcB/GTP/Mn2+ reaction, loss of the cyclic-phosphate T1 fragment accompanies rapid accumulation of the 3'-phosphate fragment above its starting background.
edges.subject: blocked-rna-cyclic-phosphate

evidence.explanation: Main Results for Figures 5-6 and visually inspected Figure 7 support the product assignment and order. The observed band is not hidden uncertainty; structural identity and a directly tracked enzyme-to-RNA GMP handoff are not independently demonstrated by this time course alone.

edges.mechanism: The delayed RNA product is assigned as the 3'-guanylylated derivative in the RtcB/GTP/Mn2+ reaction. Figures 5-6 interpretation and Figure 7 temporal ordering support this chemical step; its assignment remains explicitly inferred rather than an independently reidentified RNA structure.
edges.subject: blocked-rna-three-phosphate

causal_graphs.family_mapping: E. coli RtcB corresponds to the 408-aa P46850 reference, sequence version 3, with PF01139 at 29-408. Cited purification uses Ulp1-cleaved His10-Smt3 protein followed by nickel chromatography and gel filtration. Exact source strain and final clone sequence remain unverified; this is full-length protein, not the isolated Pfam interval.
causal_graphs.limitations: Starting RNA contains about 10% 3'-phosphate, and residual 5'-OH substrate accounts for a small ligation signal. The no-GTP control is labeled pRNAp in the caption but pRNA>p in the main text; neither identity is silently imposed, and the adopted edges use the plus-GTP time course. The specific 3'-ppG chemical assignment is inferred from mobility, GTP dependence and prior intermediate chemistry, not independently reidentified here. Enzyme-excess kinetics are not steady-state turnover.
causal_graphs.scope: Tag-free E. coli RtcB acting on a synthetic 20-mer with a 5'-phosphate and a 2',3'-cyclic phosphate; not the ligatable 5'-OH substrate or native tRNA.
causal_graphs.title: RtcB processing of a 5'-blocked cyclic-phosphate RNA substrate

causal_graphs.context: The 2012 NAR Figure 2 WT plus-GTP assay uses 50 mM Tris pH 8.0, 2 mM MnCl2, 100 uM GTP, 1 uM RtcB and 0.1 uM labeled RNA at 37 C. RNase T1 digestion reveals a six-nucleotide ligation-junction fragment. Minus-GTP and H337A panels use longer minute-scale time courses, unlike the WT plus-GTP seconds-scale panel.

evidence.explanation: Visually inspected Figure 2 and its Results identify the junction fragment and controls. Source time units and incomplete substrate cyclization are retained; slow residual hydrolysis is not mistaken for ligation.
evidence.snippet: 87% of the input substrate being ligated

edges.mechanism: The complete biochemical reaction yields the diagnostic RNase T1 fragment spanning the newly joined ends. GTP omission and H337A controls suppress efficient ligation; the graph represents the measured net reaction, not a direct one-step attack on the cyclic end.
edges.subject: rtcb-ligatable-rna-reaction

causal_graphs.family_mapping: The 408-aa E. coli RtcB is mapped to P46850 sequence version 3 and PF01139 at 29-408; experimental peptide identity and cited tag-removal protocol are retained separately. K12 is the mapped reference, not a verified experimental cloning-template strain.
causal_graphs.limitations: The substrate preparation includes about 7-8% 3'-phosphate ends, but this does not account for the much larger ligated fraction. The endpoint and time course concern synthetic RNA under enzyme excess, not turnover rates or physiological tRNA substrates. This graph is not connected directly to the 5'-blocked substrate graph. No family-wide, archaeal or mammalian cofactor independence is inferred.

record.description: This family of RNA ligases ([ec:6.5.1.3]) join 2',3'-cyclic phosphate and 5'-OH ends. They catalyse the splicing of tRNA and may also participate in tRNA repair and recovery from stress-induced RNA damage [[cite:PUB00152168],[cite:PUB00057853],[cite:PUB00056744]].

evidence.explanation: Figures 2 and 4 were visually inspected. The image/Results mass value differs from the caption, and loss-of-function mutants do not alone resolve atomic transition states.

Figures 2 and 7 were visually inspected; Figures 5-6 were assessed from Results/captions. The no-GTP control label, residual substrate species and time-axis differences remain explicit. The proposed direct cyclic-end ligation alternative is not adopted.

The cited purification protocol removes the His10-Smt3 tag before assays; the earlier protocol was checked in PMID:21224389. Neither inspection independently establishes the exact cloning-template strain.

discussions.notes: Remaining work includes exact cloning-sequence provenance, independent chemical validation of the RNA intermediate, later E. coli mechanistic studies and other members. Human/archaeal partners and cellular repair outcomes are not transferred from this bacterial system. Status remains IN_PROGRESS.
discussions.prompt: Resolve clone provenance and source-caption discrepancies, and extend member-specific ligation evidence without mixing blocked and ligatable substrates.
discussions.rationale: The protein-adduct assay, blocked-end processing time course and net ligation experiment are distinct contexts. Their combination supports a mechanistic model but is not direct tracking of one molecule through every step. One chemical-assignment edge remains INFERRED.
